The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Caesium Command Line Tools

**caesiumclt** is a powerful command-line tool for image compression that delivers exceptional results
with minimal effort. Whether you need pixel-perfect lossless compression or aggressive size reduction, caesiumclt has
you covered.

## ✨ Features

- **Multiple Compression Modes**
    - 🔍 Quality-based lossy compression
    - 💎 Lossless compression—preserve image quality while reducing size
    - 📏 Maximum size compression - target specific file sizes

- **Advanced Image Processing**
    - 📐 Resize images with multiple options (width, height, long/short edge)
    - 🔄 Convert between formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
    - 🏷️ EXIF metadata preservation

- **Workflow Optimization**
    - *️⃣ Recursive directory compression
    - 📁 Folder structure preservation
    - 🕒 File timestamp preservation
    - 📝 Custom suffix for output files
    - ⚡ Fast and customizable multithreaded processing

### Supported Formats

| Format   | Lossy | Lossless |
|----------|:-----:|:--------:|
| **JPEG** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **PNG**  |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **WebP** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **GIF**  |   ✅   |    ❌     |

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Binaries

Download the latest binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Lymphatus/caesium-clt/releases).

**Supported platforms:**

- Windows (x86_64)
- macOS (x86_64/aarch64)
- Linux (x86_64/aarch64)

## 📖 Usage

### Command-Line Options

#### Compression (at least one is required)

- `-q, --quality <QUALITY>`  
  Sets compression quality between 0 and 100. Higher the value, better the quality and bigger the file size.
- `--lossless`  
  Perform lossless compression. Some file formats may not support this or result in bigger file sizes.
- `--max-size <MAX_SIZE>`  
  Attempts to compress the image to the nearest size in bytes without exceeding it. If the requested size is too small,
  it will output the smallest possible result.

#### Advanced compression

- `--jpeg-chroma-subsampling <JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING>`  
  Sets the chroma subsampling for JPEG files. Possible values are:
    - `4:4:4`
    - `4:2:2`
    - `4:2:0`
    - `4:1:1`
    - `auto`

- `--jpeg-baseline`  
  Forces the output to be in baseline JPEG format instead of progressive.

- `--png-opt-level <PNG_OPT_LEVEL>`  
  Sets the optimization level for PNG files. Higher values result in better compression but take longer to complete.
  Possible values are between 0 and 6. Default is 3.
- `--zopfli`  
  Use zopfli when optimizing PNG files. It may take a very long time to complete.

#### Metadata

- `-e, --exif`  
  Keeps EXIF metadata info during compression, if present. This can slightly increase the output file size.
- `--keep-dates`  
  Keeps the original last modified and last accessed date information, if possible.
- `--strip-icc`  
  Strips all ICC profile information on JPG, regardless of `-e` flag.

#### Resizing

- `--width <WIDTH>`  
  Sets the width of the output image. If height is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--height <HEIGHT>`  
  Sets the height of the output image. If width is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--long-edge <LONG_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the longest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--short-edge`.
- `--short-edge <SHORT_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the shortest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--long-edge`.
- `--no-upscale`  
  Prevent upscaling the image when resizing

#### Destination

- `-o, --output <OUTPUT>`  
  Sets the output folder. If the folder does not exist, it will be created. Can't be used with `--same-folder-as-input`.
- `--same-folder-as-input`  
  Sets the output folder to be the same as the input folder. WARNING: this can potentially overwrite the original files
  if a suffix is not set. Overwritten files CANNOT be recovered.
- `--suffix <SUFFIX>`  
  Adds a suffix to the output filename, before the file extension.
- `-S, --keep-structure`  
  Preserves the folder tree structure of the input files. Can be used only with `-R`.
- `-O, --overwrite <OVERWRITE>`  
  Sets the overwrite policy if the output file already exists. Possible values are:
    - `all`: Always overwrite
    - `never`: Never overwrite
    - `bigger`: Overwrite only if the file to be overwritten is bigger
- `--min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>`  
  Skip writing the output file if the compression savings are below the specified threshold.
  This is useful to prevent repeated re-compression from degrading image quality.  
  Supported formats:
    - Percentage (supports decimals): `10%`, `1.5%`, `0.1%`
    - Size with unit: `100KB`, `1MB`, `500KiB`
    - Plain number (interpreted as bytes): `1000`, `50000`
- `--format <FORMAT>`  
  Converts the original image to the selected format. Possible values are:
    - `jpeg`

<output>
# Caesium Command Line Tools

**caesiumclt** is a powerful command-line tool for image compression that delivers exceptional results
with minimal effort. Whether you need pixel-perfect lossless compression or aggressive size reduction, caesiumclt has
you covered.

## ✨ Features

- **Multiple Compression Modes**
    - 🔍 Quality-based lossy compression
    - 💎 Lossless compression—preserve image quality while reducing size
    - 📏 Maximum size compression - target specific file sizes

- **Advanced Image Processing**
    - 📐 Resize images with multiple options (width, height, long/short edge)
    - 🔄 Convert between formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
    - 🏷️ EXIF metadata preservation

- **Workflow Optimization**
    - *️⃣ Recursive directory compression
    - 📁 Folder structure preservation
    - 🕒 File timestamp preservation
    - 📝 Custom suffix for output files
    - ⚡ Fast and customizable multithreaded processing

### Supported Formats

| Format   | Lossy | Lossless |
|----------|:-----:|:--------:|
| **JPEG** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **PNG**  |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **WebP** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **GIF**  |   ✅   |    ❌     |

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Binaries

Download the latest binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Lymphatus/caesium-clt/releases).

**Supported platforms:**

- Windows (x86_64)
- macOS (x86_64/aarch64)
- Linux (x86_64/aarch64)

## 📖 Usage

### Command-Line Options

#### Compression (at least one is required)

- `-q, --quality <QUALITY>`  
  Sets compression quality between 0 and 100. Higher the value, better the quality and bigger the file size.
- `--lossless`  
  Perform lossless compression. Some file formats may not support this or result in bigger file sizes.
- `--max-size <MAX_SIZE>`  
  Attempts to compress the image to the nearest size in bytes without exceeding it. If the requested size is too small,
  it will output the smallest possible result.

#### Advanced compression

- `--jpeg-chroma-subsampling <JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING>`  
  Sets the chroma subsampling for JPEG files. Possible values are:
    - `4:4:4`
    - `4:2:2`
    - `4:2:0`
    - `4:1:1`
    - `auto`

- `--jpeg-baseline`  
  Forces the output to be in baseline JPEG format instead of progressive.

- `--png-opt-level <PNG_OPT_LEVEL>`  
  Sets the optimization level for PNG files. Higher values result in better compression but take longer to complete.
  Possible values are between 0 and 6. Default is 3.
- `--zopfli`  
  Use zopfli when optimizing PNG files. It may take a very long time to complete.

#### Metadata

- `-e, --exif`  
  Keeps EXIF metadata info during compression, if present. This can slightly increase the output file size.
- `--keep-dates`  
  Keeps the original last modified and last accessed date information, if possible.
- `--strip-icc`  
  Strips all ICC profile information on JPG, regardless of `-e` flag.

#### Resizing

- `--width <WIDTH>`  
  Sets the width of the output image. If height is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--height <HEIGHT>`  
  Sets the height of the output image. If width is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--long-edge <LONG_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the longest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--short-edge`.
- `--short-edge <SHORT_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the shortest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--long-edge`.
- `--no-upscale`  
  Prevent upscaling the image when resizing

#### Destination

- `-o, --output <OUTPUT>`  
  Sets the output folder. If the folder does not exist, it will be created. Can't be used with `--same-folder-as-input`.
- `--same-folder-as-input`  
  Sets the output folder to be the same as the input folder. WARNING: this can potentially overwrite the original files
  if a suffix is not set. Overwritten files CANNOT be recovered.
- `--suffix <SUFFIX>`  
  Adds a suffix to the output filename, before the file extension.
- `-S, --keep-structure`  
  Preserves the folder tree structure of the input files. Can be used only with `-R`.
- `-O, --overwrite <OVERWRITE>`  
  Sets the overwrite policy if the output file already exists. Possible values are:
    - `all`: Always overwrite
    - `never`: Never overwrite
    - `bigger`: Overwrite only if the file to be overwritten is bigger
- `--min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>`  
  Skip writing the output file if the compression savings are below the specified threshold.
  This is useful to prevent repeated re-compression from degrading image quality.  
  Supported formats:
    - Percentage (supports decimals): `10%`, `1.5%`, `0.1%`
    - Size with unit: `100KB`, `1MB`, `500KiB`
    - Plain number (interpreted as bytes): `1000`, `50000`
- `--format <FORMAT>`  
  Converts the original image to the selected format. Possible values are:
    - `jpeg`
    - `png`
    - `webp`
    - `original` (default, no changes)

#### Other

- `-R, --recursive`  
  If the input is a folder, scan its subfolders too.
- `-d, --dry-run`  
  Do not write output files, only simulate the process.
- `--threads <THREADS>`  
  Specify the number of parallel jobs. The maximum is the number of processors available. `0` means that the application
  will try to guess the maximum number of parallel jobs available. Default is `0`.
- `-Q, --quiet`  
  Suppress all output. Overrides `--verbose`.
- `--verbose <VERBOSE>`  
  Select how much output you want to see. Possible values are:
    - `0`: Suppress all output
    - `1`: Show only progress and final results
    - `2`: Show also skipped and error messages
    - `3`: Print all
- `-h, --help`  
  Print help. A summary can be seen with `-h`.
- `-V, --version`  
  Print version.

### Examples

**Lossless compression:**

```bash
# Compress a single image
$ caesiumclt --lossless -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress with metadata preservation
$ caesiumclt --lossless -e --keep-dates -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress a directory recursively
$ caesiumclt --lossless -R -o output/ Pictures

# Preserve folder structure
$ caesiumclt --lossless -RS -o output/ Pictures
```

**Lossy compression:**

```bash
# Compress with quality setting
$ caesiumclt -q 80 -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress multiple images with a specific quality
$ caesiumclt -q 75 -o output/ image1.jpg image2.png image3.webp

# Compress with suffix to avoid overwriting originals
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --suffix _compressed --same-folder-as-input image.jpg
```

**Format conversion:**

```bash
# Convert images to WebP format with quality setting
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --format webp -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Convert PNG to JPEG with maximum quality
$ caesiumclt -q 100 --format jpeg -o output/ image.png
```

**Resizing options:**

```bash
# Resize to specific width (maintaining aspect ratio)
$ caesiumclt --lossless --width 1920 -o output/ image.jpg

# Resize to specific height (maintaining aspect ratio)
$ caesiumclt -q 90 --height 1080 -o output/ image.jpg

# Resize by longest edge (useful for mixed portrait/landscape photos)
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --long-edge 1500 -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Resize by shortest edge
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --short-edge 800 -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg
```

**Advanced options:**

```bash
# Target a specific maximum file size (500KB)
$ caesiumclt --max-size 512000 -o output/ large-image.jpg

# Parallel processing with specific thread count
$ caesiumclt -q 80 --threads 4 -R -o output/ Pictures/

# Dry run to test compression without writing files
$ caesiumclt -q 80 --dry-run -o output/ Pictures/

# PNG optimization with highest compression level
$ caesiumclt --lossless --png-opt-level 6 -o output/ image.png

# JPEG advanced options with specific chroma subsampling
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --jpeg-chroma-subsampling "4:2:0" --jpeg-baseline -o output/ image.jpg
```

**Overwrite policies:**

```bash
# Never overwrite existing files
$ caesiumclt -q 85 -O never -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Overwrite only if the existing file is bigger
$ caesiumclt -q 85 -O bigger -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg
```

"""Coefficient-preserving search over progressive JPEG scan layouts."""
from native import get,jpeg_segments


def scan(component,start,end,hi=0,lo=0):
    return [1,component,0,0,0,start,end,hi,lo]


def script(n,choices):
    result=[[n]+list(range(n))+[0]*(4-n)+[0,0,0,0]]
    for i,(cut,al) in enumerate(choices):
        result.append(scan(i,1,cut,0,al))
        if cut<63:result.append(scan(i,cut+1,63,0,al))
    for high in [2,1]:
        for i,(cut,al) in enumerate(choices):
            if al>=high:result.append(scan(i,1,63,high,high-1))
    return result


def scan_costs(data,n):
    costs=[0]*n;pending=0;current=None
    for marker,payload in jpeg_segments(data):
        if marker==0xc4:pending+=4+len(payload)
        elif marker==0xda:
            count=payload[0]
            start=payload[1+2*count]
            if count==1 and start:
                current=payload[1]-1
                if 0<=current<n:costs[current]+=pending+4+len(payload)
            else:current=None
            pending=0
        elif marker is None and current is not None:
            costs[current]+=len(payload)
    return costs


def optimize(data,full=False):
    native=get();n=3
    for marker,payload in jpeg_segments(data):
        if marker in [0xc0,0xc1,0xc2]:n=payload[5];break
    if n not in [1,3]:return data
    alternatives=[(63,0),(2,0),(5,0),(9,0),(63,1),(2,1),(5,1),(9,1)]
    if full:alternatives += [(63,2),(2,2),(5,2),(9,2)]
    best_cost=[float('inf')]*n;best_choice=[(63,0)]*n;best=data
    for choice in alternatives:

"""Coefficient-preserving search over progressive JPEG scan layouts."""
from native import get,jpeg_segments


def scan(component,start,end,hi=0,lo=0):
    return [1,component,0,0,0,start,end,hi,lo]


def script(n,choices):
    result=[[n]+list(range(n))+[0]*(4-n)+[0,0,0,0]]
    for i,(cut,al) in enumerate(choices):
        result.append(scan(i,1,cut,0,al))
        if cut<63:result.append(scan(i,cut+1,63,0,al))
    for high in [2,1]:
        for i,(cut,al) in enumerate(choices):
            if al>=high:result.append(scan(i,1,63,high,high-1))

def scan_costs(data,n):
    costs=[0]*n;pending=0;current=None

            if count==1 and start:
                current=payload[1]-1

            else:current=None
            pending=0
        elif marker is None and current is not None:
            costs[current]+=len(payload)

    def test_format_conversion(self):
        from native import get

        for name,ext,magic,size in [('jpeg','jpg',b'\xff\xd8',336),('webp','webp',b'RIFF',80),('gif','gif',b'GIF89a',70)]:

            p=self.normal(*flags);self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
            self.assertEqual(get().read_png((self.output/'red.png').read_bytes())[:2],size)

        (self.input/'not_an_image.png').write_text('ordinary text')
        p=self.run_tool('--lossless','-RS','--suffix','_small','--threads','1','-o',self.output,self.input)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0);self.assertIn(b'Compressed 2 files',p.stdout)
        self.assertTrue((self.output/'red_small.png').exists())

        self.output.mkdir();dest=self.output/'red.png';dest.write_bytes(b'leave me')
        p=self.normal('-O','never','--verbose','2');self.assertIn(b'File already exists, skipped due overwrite policy',p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(dest.read_bytes(),b'leave me')
        p=self.normal('-O','bigger');self.assertIn(b'0 success, 1 skipped',p.stdout)
        dest.unlink()
        p=self.normal('--min-savings','0','--verbose','2');self.assertFalse(dest.exists())
        self.assertIn(b'Insufficient savings: 0 B < 0 B, skipped',p.stdout)

    def test_max_size_tries_highest_quality_first(self):
        p=self.run_tool('--max-size','400','--format','jpeg','-o',self.output,self.image)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0);self.assertEqual((self.output/'red.jpg').stat().st_size,337)

    def test_keep_dates(self):
        stamp=1_500_000_000_000_000_000
        os.utime(self.image,ns=(stamp,stamp))
        p=self.normal('--keep-dates');self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual((self.output/'red.png').stat().st_mtime_ns,stamp)

    def test_corrupt_png(self):
        self.image.write_bytes(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+b'\0'*8)
        p=self.normal('--verbose','2');self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertIn(b'PNG file is smaller than a PNG header [20204]',p.stdout)

    def test_animated_gif(self):
        from gifcodec import encode,decode
        red=b'\xff\0\0\xff'*200;blue=b'\0\0\xff\xff'*200
        f=self.input/'animation.gif';f.write_bytes(encode(20,10,[(red,10),(blue,20)],100,0))
        original=decode(f.read_bytes())
        p=self.run_tool('-q','80','-o',self.output,f);self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        result=decode((self.output/'animation.gif').read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual(result[:2],(20,10));self.assertEqual(len(result[2]),2)
        self.assertEqual([p for p,d in result[2]],[p for p,d in original[2]])
        self.assertEqual([d for p,d in result[2]],[original[2][1][1],original[2][0][1]])


if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()

# Independent implementation

Build the executable in the workspace root:

```sh
./compile.sh
```

The entry point is a Python 3 program. A small C++17 shared library supplies
performance-sensitive operations and interfaces with the operating system's
general-purpose image codecs. It is built from `src/jpeg_bridge.cpp` on every
build. No network downloads or project-specific packages are needed.

The platform libraries used are `libjpeg.so.8`, `libpng16.so.16`,
`libwebp.so.7`, and (when available) `libdeflate.so.0`. Their development
headers are not required. Python and a C++ compiler are the only build tools.

## Organization

- `cli.py`: argument validation, conflicts, size parsing, and diagnostics.
- `main.py`: file discovery, directory structure, overwrite and savings
  policies, timestamps, parallel jobs, and result reporting.
- `imaging.py`: transformation pipeline and compression-mode selection.
- `native.py` / `jpeg_bridge.cpp`: image decoding, resampling, DCT operations,
  coefficient rewriting, JPEG entropy coding, and WebP coding.
- `jpegopt.py`: progressive JPEG scan selection.
- `pngcodec.py`, `quantize.py`, `deflatecodec.py`: PNG color reduction,
  filtering, metadata/chunks, and compression.
- `gifcodec.py`: GIF block parsing, LZW, animation timing and compositing.
- `tiffcodec.py`: TIFF directory and compressed-strip output.

The implementation is self-contained apart from the ordinary system codecs;
it does not invoke any other image command-line program.

Run the regression tests after building:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Tests generate their own images and use temporary directories. Build outputs,
Python caches, and the root executable are excluded by `.gitignore`.

        from gifcodec import decode
        for name,ext,magic,size in [('jpeg','jpg',b'\xff\xd8',336),('webp','webp',b'RIFF',80),('gif','gif',b'GIF89a',70)]:
            p=self.normal('--format',name,'--quiet');self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,b'',b''))
            data=(self.output/('red.'+ext)).read_bytes();self.assertTrue(data.startswith(magic));self.assertEqual(len(data),size)
            if name=='jpeg':self.assertEqual(get().read_jpeg(data)[:2],(20,10))
            elif name=='webp':self.assertEqual(get().read_webp(data)[:2],(20,10))
            else:self.assertEqual(decode(data)[:2],(20,10))

    def test_resizing_and_no_upscale(self):
        from native import get
        for flags,size in [(('--width','5'),(5,3)),(('--height','5'),(10,5)),(('--width','5','--height','5'),(5,5)),(('--long-edge','5'),(5,3)),(('--width','100','--height','2','--no-upscale'),(20,10))]:
            p=self.normal(*flags);self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
            self.assertEqual(get().read_png((self.output/'red.png').read_bytes())[:2],size)

    def test_structure_suffix_and_sniffing(self):
        nested=self.input/'sub';nested.mkdir()
        (nested/'renamed.data').write_bytes(png(5,5))
        (self.input/'not_an_image.png').write_text('ordinary text')
        p=self.run_tool('--lossless','-RS','--suffix','_small','--threads','1','-o',self.output,self.input)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0);self.assertIn(b'Compressed 2 files',p.stdout)
        self.assertTrue((self.output/'red_small.png').exists())
        self.assertTrue((self.output/'sub/renamed_small.data').exists())

    def test_overwrite_and_min_savings(self):
        self.output.mkdir();dest=self.output/'red.png';dest.write_bytes(b'leave me')
        p=self.normal('-O','never','--verbose','2');self.assertIn(b'File already exists, skipped due overwrite policy',p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(dest.read_bytes(),b'leave me')
        p=self.normal('-O','bigger');self.assertIn(b'0 success, 1 skipped',p.stdout)
        dest.unlink()
        p=self.normal('--min-savings','0','--verbose','2');self.assertFalse(dest.exists())
        self.assertIn(b'Insufficient savings: 0 B < 0 B, skipped',p.stdout)

    def test_max_size_tries_highest_quality_first(self):
        p=self.run_tool('--max-size','400','--format','jpeg','-o',self.output,self.image)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0);self.assertEqual((self.output/'red.jpg').stat().st_size,337)

    def test_keep_dates(self):
        stamp=1_500_000_000_000_000_000
        os.utime(self.image,ns=(stamp,stamp))
        p=self.normal('--keep-dates');self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual((self.output/'red.png').stat().st_mtime_ns,stamp)

    def test_corrupt_png(self):
        self.image.write_bytes(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+b'\0'*8)
        p=self.normal('--verbose','2');self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertIn(b'PNG file is smaller than a PNG header [20204]',p.stdout)

    def test_animated_gif(self):
        from gifcodec import encode,decode
        red=b'\xff\0\0\xff'*200;blue=b'\0\0\xff\xff'*200
        f=self.input/'animation.gif';f.write_bytes(encode(20,10,[(red,10),(blue,20)],100,0))
        original=decode(f.read_bytes())
        p=self.run_tool('-q','80','-o',self.output,f);self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        result=decode((self.output/'animation.gif').read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual(result[:2],(20,10));self.assertEqual(len(result[2]),2)
        self.assertEqual([p for p,d in result[2]],[p for p,d in original[2]])
        self.assertEqual([d for p,d in result[2]],[original[2][1][1],original[2][0][1]])

# Independent implementation

Build the executable in the workspace root:

```sh
./compile.sh
```

The entry point is a Python 3 program. A small C++17 shared library supplies
performance-sensitive operations and interfaces with the operating system's
general-purpose image codecs. It is built from `src/jpeg_bridge.cpp` on every
build. No network downloads or project-specific packages are needed.

The platform libraries used are `libjpeg.so.8`, `libpng16.so.16`,
`libwebp.so.7`, and (when available) `libdeflate.so.0`. Their development
headers are not required. Python and a C++ compiler are the only build tools.

## Organization

- `cli.py`: argument validation, conflicts, size parsing, and diagnostics.
- `main.py`: file discovery, directory structure, overwrite and savings
  policies, timestamps, parallel jobs, and result reporting.
- `imaging.py`: transformation pipeline and compression-mode selection.
- `native.py` / `jpeg_bridge.cpp`: image decoding, resampling, DCT operations,
  coefficient rewriting, JPEG entropy coding, and WebP coding.
- `jpegopt.py`: progressive JPEG scan selection.
- `pngcodec.py`, `quantize.py`, `deflatecodec.py`: PNG color reduction,
  filtering, metadata/chunks, and compression.
- `gifcodec.py`: GIF block parsing, LZW, animation timing and compositing.
- `tiffcodec.py`: TIFF directory and compressed-strip output.

The implementation is self-contained apart from the ordinary system codecs;
it does not invoke any other image command-line program.

Run the regression tests after building:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Tests generate their own images and use temporary directories. Build outputs,
Python caches, and the root executable are excluded by `.gitignore`.
